evidence.excerpt: Online travel agencies have made price dispersion in tourism accommodation highly visible to consumers, yet its structural determinants remain understudied in South-East European contexts. This study draws on a scraped dataset of 4,200 daily rate observations from a single mid-size online travel agency covering 112 Dalmatian coastal hotels during the summer seasons of 2008 and 2009. Quantile regression estimates reveal that price dispersion at the upper tail is driven primarily by star-rating heterogeneity and last-minute inventory clearance, while dispersion at the lower tail reflects competitive pressure from unlicensed accommodation. A price-concentration index constructed for 14 micro-destinations shows significant variation even within the same coastal stretch. The findings suggest that revenue managers in the region treat promotional discounting and peak-period premiums as largely independent decisions, which limits overall yield performance.
